title: Use of xanthan gum in dietary management of diabetes mellitus
authors: Osilesi O, Trout DL, Glover EE, Harper SM, Koh ET, Behall KM, et al.
journal: The American Journal of Clinical Nutrition
followUp: 12 weeks of muffin feeding, xanthan gum during one half
population: Nine free-living people with diabetes, with moderately raised serum glucose and managed without insulin or hypoglycaemic drugs, and four people without diabetes
funder: not readable. The full text is behind a paywall and no open copy was located; the PubMed record lists no grant support and indexes the paper as Research Support, U.S. Gov't, Non-P.H.S.
result: Xanthan gum 12 g per day was fed in muffins during either the first or the second half of a 12-week muffin-feeding period. Blood was taken before the study and at the end of the xanthan and xanthan-free periods, before and 2 hours after an oral glucose load. In the participants with diabetes, feeding xanthan gum lowered fasting and post-load serum glucose and fasting total plasma cholesterol, and tended to lower fasting and post-load gastrin and gastric inhibitory polypeptide and fasting total and VLDL triglyceride and cholesterol in the VLDL and LDL fractions. Participants reported fullness after the xanthan muffins and no severe digestive symptoms. The abstract, the only part readable, reports directions of effect without figures; EFSA's re-evaluations of xanthan gum do not cite this study.
